speaker: josias_thwaite
text: We shall be brief, brethren.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Ten days to the fast. Ash Wednesday is the fifth of March. I have counted them once. The glass will make me count them again.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Brief, he says. The glass is on the pulpit, and he will turn it. He turns it twice. He always has.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then let him turn it. I can hear a man and still know what day the fast begins.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Sir John is three rows ahead, in the carved pew, and he has not turned his head.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him his pew. He has nothing to say to me, and I will not call across the aisle.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: I turn the glass. Once. You that came for a short morning have the second turning still to come.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: There is the first. Sit still, Alse. Dinner will wait. Fidgeting will not hurry a sermon.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The loaf was short by a finger. Sitting still will not lengthen it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A penny, and short by a finger. That is the baker. It is not Master Thwaite.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Ten days. The parish turns toward the fast. I will not hurry the parish because a player is counting a play.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am counting ten, sir. I can do that and hear you.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Hear him, then. Last Sunday your mouth was working a scene of your own. Not today.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib is on a book at home. I shut the door on him. He will still be on it when we are back.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let the cat keep the page. I am not going up for it between the two glasses.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: The second turning. We are not done because the aisle is hungry, Mistress Ansell.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I am hungry at the right hour, and I will wait the second glass. I did not come to argue with the pulpit.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good. Argue with me at dinner, if you must argue. Today the house can have an ordinary Sunday.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Ordinary is dinner and the washing-up. I can do ordinary.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You will do the washing-up after we have eaten, and not before. Master Shakespeare pays threepence when he sits at my board. Mark me.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Threepence for his dinner, and the sixpence for firing and washing with it. Once this week. I will not have it asked on Monday as if it were new.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: The fast is not today. Today you may eat. In ten days you may remember that I told you the number.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Ten. I can remember ten if someone says it often enough.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: He has said it often enough. When he releases us, we go by the south door, as we came.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The south aisle, Mistress. I came in with you. Sir John may keep his head where it is.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: I have spent the two glasses. Go to your dinners. Ten days, and then the fast. That is the morning's arithmetic.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Ten days. I have it. Alse, the cloak. Master Shakespeare, you are not to linger in the porch and call it prayer.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will count the days on my fingers, and then I will come to table.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: That is ten fingers, sir. You will not need a book for it.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Go. The parish has not been brief, and it has been told the number. Dinner is your affair now, not mine.
